top.en: Actually, after 2022, the club could have rotated ShowMaker and brought in a new mid laner. Canyon also saw that ShowMaker's form had declined significantly. They played 'brother LoL' for so long, and in the end, they were 'selling tickets' at Worlds. There's no point in continuing to play. The most ridiculous thing is that the club signed Deft and Aiming at high prices in the twilight of their careers [facepalm]. Kingen, they spent all the money and didn't get good results. Later, the sponsors stopped investing, and they had to rely on ShowMaker to save face and attract viewers. Later, they used many players for top, jungle, ADC, and support like Perfect, Kingen, Siwoo, Lucas, Deft, Aiming, Smash, Moham, BeryL, Kellin, etc. The coaching staff was also changed wave after wave, but there were no good results in major tournaments. You don't need to ask whose problem it is [facepalm]. Who says Korea doesn't have this? It's just that this year the club started owing salaries and felt like it was going to disband, so they only managed to win the Esports World Cup, but overall the losses are already too big.

So BLG decided not to care about laning strength in the draft, believing player skill could compensate. They focused entirely on the scaling curves. It feels like IG vs TES, exactly the same. Still, don't pop the champagne yet, stay vigilant.

top.en: If you don't understand the draft, just go watch Chu Jun's video on Bilibili. He completely predicted every direction and detail of the draft. The coaches and players must have analyzed DK's gameplay and realized their laning phase is average, and they like to play for the late game and teamfight comebacks. So BLG decided not to care about lane strength in the draft, whether they were ahead or behind, trusting that player skill could make up for it. The focus was entirely on the team composition's scaling curve—mid-to-late game comps. But who knew that once in-game, even with a winning draft, the opponent couldn't win? They didn't even get a dragon in two games with winning lanes, and instead, BLG took a bunch of dragons. It feels just like IG vs TES, exactly the same. These two teams must have been scrimming each other; the draft direction and game content are identical. Both are weak-lane comps, but once in-game, they rely on player ability and individual star power to turn losing matchups into winning ones. It's insane. Still, no popping champagne yet, stay vigilant.
